content.title: Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen Review: Netflix's Twisted & Gory Horror Will Leave You Reeling
content.text: Every horror lover needs to check out Netflix’s Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen, a top-notch series that will leave you reeling long after it's finished. Horror has become a staple on TV, and streaming services have jumped at the chance to leave viewers with chills and thrills. One of my favorite additions in a long time is the Netflix show Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen. The Duffer Brothers get most of the attention for co-producing the Stranger Things follow-up. However, an equally important individual on the creative team is Haley Z. Boston, the brilliant creator, writer, and showrunner behind the Netflix horror show. Boston told Tudum that she wanted to tap into the visceral terror of marrying the wrong person. Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen’s Story Is Almost Perfect Something Very Bad is Going to Happen starts with a seemingly straightforward premise. The story centers on a young woman named Rachel (Camila Morrone), who agrees to marry her boyfriend Nicky (Adam DiMarco) at his family's remote cabin. However, her paranoia grows as the ill-fated wedding approaches, leading her to believe something sinister is at play. Despite the simple concept, Netflix's horror show never lets the viewer get too comfortable. There’s always another twist. There’s always another character reveal. The plot forces the audience to decide who they can and cannot trust, and it's never easy. Pretty much everyone's acting sketchy. Despite the incredible story and character developments, the Netflix series wasn’t without a couple of issues. The show set up a few weird story elements that they completely forgot to address. Netflix’s Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen Blends Together Many Forms Of Horror Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 The Duffer Brothers’ new show on Netflix is creepy, twisted, and all things spooky. The strength of Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen lies in its ability to draw on both horror tropes and techniques without feeling derivative or boring. On the narrative side, the Netflix series weaves together a cabin-in-the-woods, a creepy family, a spooky seance, and other horror tropes that would spoil major twists. I appreciated that the series draws inspiration from Gothic authors such as Johann Wolfgang von Goethe and Shirley Jackson. What's more, it feels like an homage rather than a ripoff because it makes enough changes to feel unique. The opening scene of the show sets the immediate expectation that the Netflix series will be filled with blood and gore, and boy, does it follow through in the best way. The creative team throws in moments of shocking gore and body horror. The narrow and long hallways in Nicky’s family’s house induce a feeling of claustrophobia and inescapability. Isolation from the outside world, minus the bar, increases these feelings. The Netflix show occasionally even uses fakeouts, creating uncertainty about when fear is warranted and when everything’s safe. The Duffer Brothers’ New Netflix Show Is A Masterclass In Cinematography, Scoring, & SFX As incredible as the story is in Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen, I was even more enthralled by the technical achievements. The series blends a realistic film style with elements of expressionism and includes a couple of episodes in a naturalistic found-footage style. On top of that, lighting heavily influences the mood of each scene. For instance, the bar features heavy shadows, dimness, and neon colors. Later, the more dramatic moments use candlelight. In both of these examples, the scene would have felt entirely different in different lighting. I found this kind of intentionality and thought in every frame. The Duffer Brothers’ Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen will go down in history as one of the best Netflix horror shows of all time. Moreover, the opening scene of the show sets the immediate expectation that the Netflix series will be filled with blood and gore, and boy, does it follow through in the best way. The VFX makes these moments look shockingly realistic. Just a tip, I would not recommend watching Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen while eating because some of the gore is stomach-churning. Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen Is Among The Best Netflix Horrors Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 Taking everything into consideration, Netflix needs to make space for Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen alongside its all-time greats. Not only is the series award-worthy, but it also ranks highly on the list of the best Netflix horror shows. It's as if the show collected all the strengths of its predecessors. Even with the minor narrative issues mentioned previously, The Duffer Brothers’ Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen will go down in history as one of the best Netflix horror shows of all time.
